claims.title: Shopper order details may be intercepted if storefront transport is not encrypted
claims.description: `flow:entity:shopper>process:storefront-api>place-order` crosses from `boundary:public-internet` to `process:storefront-api` and carries order contents, shipping addresses, and card last-four. Its `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If that attribute resolves to no effective TLS protection, an on-path attacker reads shoppers' PII and financial order data in transit. The disclosed address and order details can then enable targeted fraud or social engineering against `entity:shopper`.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because the public-to-DMZ flow crosses a trust boundary but `encryption_in_transit` and protocol are unstated. Impact is high because the flow carries PII and financial order data, and a path observer can capture many shoppers' transactions.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce TLS for shopper order submission
mitigations.detail: Set `encryption_in_transit` on `flow:entity:shopper>process:storefront-api>place-order` to TLS 1.2+ and reject plaintext or downgrade-capable connections.

claims.title: Settlement callbacks may disclose payment status if webhook transport is unprotected
claims.description: `flow:entity:card-processor>process:storefront-api>settlement-webhook` crosses from the public internet to the internet-facing `process:storefront-api` and carries a financial settlement confirmation. Its protocol and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown. If the callback is not protected by TLS, an on-path observer can intercept order-payment status and correlate it with later order-processing activity; this gives an attacker payment intelligence useful for targeting orders and shoppers.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because this is a public-boundary callback but both protocol and transport encryption are unstated. Impact is medium because the flow is tagged financial and reveals settlement information, though the described payload is limited to an order confirmation.

mitigations.detail: Document and enforce TLS 1.2+ on `flow:entity:card-processor>process:storefront-api>settlement-webhook`, including certificate validation at the processor and storefront endpoints.

claims.title: Order payloads may be readable on the unverified DMZ-to-core gRPC channel
claims.description: `flow:process:storefront-api>process:order-service>submit-order` crosses from `boundary:storefront-dmz` to `boundary:core-services` and carries order contents, shopper identifiers, and shipping addresses. Its `encryption_in_transit` is unknown; separately, the destination accepts the call without authentication. If transport encryption is absent or ineffective, an attacker able to observe the DMZ-to-core path can intercept PII and financial order data without needing the service's application credentials. Those identifiers can subsequently be used to target records held by `store:orders-db` or the affected shoppers.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unverified transport, since an attacker must gain observation of the DMZ-to-core route. Impact is high because this boundary-crossing flow continuously carries PII and financial order data.

mitigations.summary: Use mTLS for the storefront-to-order-service gRPC call
mitigations.detail: Set `encryption_in_transit` to mutually authenticated TLS on `flow:process:storefront-api>process:order-service>submit-order` so payload confidentiality and peer identity are both enforced.

mitigations.summary: Minimize sensitive fields forwarded to the order service
mitigations.detail: Replace shopper identifiers and address data with opaque order references where the downstream service can resolve them safely.

claims.title: Order database traffic may expose the confidential order corpus in transit
claims.description: `flow:process:order-service>store:orders-db>read-write-orders` carries order rows, shipping addresses, and card last-four to confidential `store:orders-db`, but both its protocol and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown. If this database connection lacks effective transport encryption, an attacker with visibility into the core-services path can intercept database requests and responses, including shopper PII and financial data. Captured records enable targeted abuse against `entity:shopper` and reveal the structure needed to target the order corpus.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because observing an internal database path requires a foothold, while protocol and transport encryption are unstated. Impact is high because the destination is confidential and the flow carries PII and financial order records.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt and authenticate the database connection
mitigations.detail: Require TLS with server certificate validation for `flow:process:order-service>store:orders-db>read-write-orders`; use mTLS where supported.

claims.title: Receipt contents may be readable in transit because the model and source disagree on TLS
claims.description: `flow:process:order-service>store:receipt-archive>append-receipt` is modeled with `encryption_in_transit` absent, but the source states that the receipt write is on TLS; the catalog records this as a disagreement. If the modeled absent state is correct, an on-path attacker can intercept receipt objects identifying the order written and the writing service. This is conditional on resolving the contradictory transport statements and can disclose order-processing metadata useful for correlating order activity.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because an attacker needs access to the internal path and the source/model TLS posture conflicts. Impact is medium because intercepted receipts disclose order-processing metadata and the flow is associated with business-critical and financial order activity.

mitigations.summary: Resolve and enforce the receipt transport configuration
mitigations.detail: Verify the effective configuration for `flow:process:order-service>store:receipt-archive>append-receipt`, record TLS as the verified transport control, and fail connections that cannot validate the storage endpoint.

claims.title: A storage copy of orders-db may expose confidential shopper and payment data
claims.description: `store:orders-db` is classified confidential and holds shopper addresses and card last-four, with `pii` and `financial` assets, but its `encryption_at_rest` state is unknown. If at-rest encryption is not enabled for the database and its operational copies, an attacker who obtains a volume, snapshot, backup, or decommissioned storage copy can read the order corpus without using `process:order-service` or its database account. The disclosure enables bulk targeting of `entity:shopper` and is irreversible once copied.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown at-rest control: obtaining a storage copy is a prerequisite, but an unencrypted copy requires no live database access. Impact is high because `store:orders-db` is confidential and holds PII and financial data for the order corpus.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce encryption at rest for orders-db and copies
mitigations.detail: Establish the `encryption_at_rest` posture of `store:orders-db`; use managed or customer-managed keys for database media, backups, snapshots, replicas, and exports, and restrict export and key-use permissions.

mitigations.summary: Protect the most sensitive fields separately
mitigations.detail: Apply field-level encryption or tokenization to shopper addresses and payment-related columns where operationally feasible.

claims.title: Receipt archive copies may be readable at rest if the modeled encryption gap is correct
claims.description: `store:receipt-archive` is modeled with `encryption_at_rest` absent, while the source states that the bucket is encrypted with a customer-managed key; the evidence catalog records this as a disagreement. If the modeled absent state is correct, an attacker holding a bucket export, storage copy, or backup can read receipts without using the order service's account. This is conditional on resolving the conflicting storage-encryption facts; the receipts reveal order-processing records and can be correlated with other order activity.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because an attacker must obtain a storage copy and the source/model encryption state conflicts. Impact is medium because the archive stores one receipt per completed order, although its classification is unknown.

mitigations.summary: Reconcile the receipt archive encryption posture
mitigations.detail: Verify that `store:receipt-archive` uses the stated customer-managed key and that encryption covers all object versions, backups, exports, and recovery copies.

mitigations.summary: Classify receipts and restrict storage-copy access
mitigations.detail: Set a verified data classification for `store:receipt-archive` and limit bucket export, backup, and key-decrypt permissions to dedicated operational principals.

claims.title: Compromised order-service code can read the full orders database through its broad application grant
claims.description: `process:order-service` reads and writes `store:orders-db` through `flow:process:order-service>store:orders-db>read-write-orders`, using one application account with full read/write authority. An attacker who obtains code execution or host control in `process:order-service` can use that already-authorized database session to read the full confidential corpus of addresses and card last-four, rather than only records needed for one order. This is distinct from a storage-copy threat because database at-rest encryption would not stop an authorized application session. The harvested data enables bulk targeting of `entity:shopper`.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low because the attacker must first compromise the internal `process:order-service`; however, the stated application account then already has full read/write authority. Impact is high because `store:orders-db` is confidential and contains PII and financial data across the order corpus.

mitigations.summary: Replace the full-database application grant with least privilege
mitigations.detail: Split the application account into narrowly scoped roles and limit `process:order-service` to the tables, rows, and columns needed for order capture and receipt generation.

mitigations.summary: Detect anomalous reads by the order-service account
mitigations.detail: Log database query identity and volume, alert on bulk extraction patterns, and separate read permissions from write permissions where possible.

claims.title: The static order-service database password can be recovered from the worker environment and reused to read orders
claims.description: The password used by the application account on `flow:process:order-service>store:orders-db>read-write-orders` is kept in an environment variable on `process:order-service`, and that account has full read/write authority to `store:orders-db`. An attacker who obtains the worker environment, such as through a deployment, diagnostic, image, or runtime exposure, can recover the standing credential and present it to read the confidential order corpus. The resulting PII and card-last-four disclosure enables bulk targeting of `entity:shopper` and persists until the password is rotated.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium because recovering an environment variable requires access to the worker environment, but the credential is a standing password rather than a short-lived identity. Impact is high because the recovered credential carries full read/write access to confidential `store:orders-db` containing PII and financial data.

mitigations.summary: Remove the standing password from the worker environment
mitigations.detail: Use workload identity or short-lived database credentials issued through a dedicated secret-management system rather than an environment-variable password.

mitigations.summary: Rotate and constrain the database credential
mitigations.detail: Rotate the current application-account password, remove full read/write access, and issue separate narrowly scoped credentials for required operations.
